# EchoLearn — yt-dlp transcript service (VPS)

A tiny FastAPI service that fetches YouTube transcripts with
[yt-dlp](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp) and returns them in the exact
shape the EchoLearn web app and CF Worker expect:

```json
{
  "lines": [{ "id": "yt_1", "start": 0.0, "end": 1.23, "text": "..." }],
  "language": "en",
  "isAutoGenerated": false
}
```

## Why this exists

The CF Worker (datacenter IP) and the user's local proxy were the only paths
to captions. This service runs on a cheap always-on VPS. yt-dlp rotates
YouTube client signatures (web / android / tv / ios) and the `TVHTML5` client
bypasses YouTube's datacenter-IP bot check, so **captions work without a
residential proxy for most videos**. The user's PC no longer has to stay on.

## Endpoints

- `GET /api/transcript?videoId=<id>&lang=<en>` — transcript JSON
- `GET /api/health` — liveness check (no yt-dlp call)

## Run it

### Option A — plain Python (simplest)

```bash
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
uvicorn main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
```

### Option B — Docker

```bash
docker build -t echolearn-ytdlp .
docker run -d --restart unless-stopped -p 8000:8000 echolearn-ytdlp
```

### Run as a systemd service (recommended for a VPS)

```ini
# /etc/systemd/system/echolearn-ytdlp.service
[Unit]
Description=EchoLearn yt-dlp transcript service
After=network.target

[Service]
WorkingDirectory=/opt/echolearn-ytdlp
ExecStart=/opt/echolearn-ytdlp/.venv/bin/uvicorn main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000
Restart=always
Environment=YTDLP_TIMEOUT=90

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

```bash
sudo systemctl enable --now echolearn-ytdlp
```

## Environment variables

| Var | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `YTDLP_TIMEOUT` | `90` | Hard timeout (s) for the yt-dlp subprocess |
| `YTDLP_PROXY` | _(empty)_ | Upstream proxy passed to yt-dlp (e.g. a residential proxy endpoint). Use only if YouTube blocks even the TVHTML5 client from your VPS IP |
| `YTDLP_API_KEY` | _(empty)_ | If set, `/api/transcript` requires header `X-Api-Key` to match. Set this **and** the Worker's `YTDLP_API_KEY` to the same value |

## Expose it to the CF Worker

The VPS should be reachable over HTTPS at a stable URL. Since the project
already uses Cloudflare:

1. Add a DNS `A` record, e.g. `yt-api.echo-learn.uk` → your VPS public IP.
2. Set the Cloudflare proxy (orange cloud) on so Cloudflare terminates TLS;
   your origin can stay plain HTTP on port 8000.
3. In the CF Worker, set the secret:

   ```bash
   npx wrangler secret put YTDLP_API_URL   # value: https://yt-api.echo-learn.uk
   # optional, recommended:
   npx wrangler secret put YTDLP_API_KEY   # same value as the VPS YTDLP_API_KEY
   npx wrangler deploy
   ```

The Worker now tries this service first for every server-side transcript
request. If it returns nothing, the Worker falls through to its other
strategies. The user's local proxy (client-side) is still attempted before
the Worker, so it remains the primary when the user's PC is online.

## Notes / limits

- **Captions only.** For videos with *no* caption track at all, set
  `YTDLP_PROXY` to a residential proxy (the unused Proxy-Cheap order works
  here) so yt-dlp can download audio for Whisper — or let users upload an
  SRT/VTT manually in the app.
- Keep yt-dlp updated: `pip install -U yt-dlp`. YouTube changes often; the
  community fixes it within hours.
- A 1 vCPU / 1 GB VPS is plenty — yt-dlp is lightweight.
